headline: 27 resolved trades, net -2.1 bps/bet (-56.1 bps total); last-10 window +9.6 bps net. Still too thin to judge.
regime_note: BTC ~$75.6k, holding the higher-price band (~$76-81k) where recent fills have skewed positive; the deep-losing cluster sits earlier at $63-66k. Signal currently flat (0).
assessment_md:
**How it's doing:** Over the full live ledger of 27 trades, the strategy is net negative: -2.1 bps per bet, -56.1 bps cumulative, winning just 37% of the time. That's below the marginal ~4 bps gross edge we expected — but on a sample this small, that gap is well within noise.

**What changed vs last time:** The ledger is unchanged (still 27 resolved trades), so no new information has accumulated at the top level. What's worth noting is the recent tone: the trailing 10-bet window is net **+9.6 bps** (gross 12.6, 70% win rate), driven by good short fills in the $77-81k band (e.g. +48.7, +25.9, +25.3 bps). The big losers (-28, -13, -13 bps) are concentrated earlier, mostly at $63-66k.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us:** They tell us the sample is still far too small to conclude anything. 27 trades with two or three outliers dominating the total means neither the -56 bps nor the recent +9.6 bps window is statistically meaningful. This strategy was always marginal — ~4 bps gross edge vs ~3.9 bps breakeven cost — and independent edge-search found **zero** survivors passing a stricter 5 bps two-venue bar.

**Bottom line:** No edge is proven, and none should be assumed. The recent bounce is encouraging but not evidence. Keep collecting data; do not size up. This is not a profitable signal until many dozens more trades say otherwise.
